mainTopic: How the person 'whose words were not fulfilled' can be a נזיר (אביי's answer), and an inference from the משנה's case of the man who turned back
overview: The משנה (נזיר 32b) describes people who see someone approaching from far away. Each one vows to be a נזיר depending on who the man turns out to be. בית הלל rule that only the one 'whose words were not fulfilled' becomes a נזיר, which sounds backwards. אביי explains that this speaker also said, 'even if it is not so-and-so, I am a נזיר.' So 'not fulfilled' means only his first words failed, and his last words came true. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's next line: if the approaching man turned back and was never identified, no one is a נזיר. From this it infers that if the man had come close and been identified, the one who vowed would be a נזיר. The גמרא asks whose opinion this follows, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי explains how 'not fulfilled' can still make someone a nazir
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the משנה as a case where the speaker added 'even if it is not so-and-so, I am a נזיר.' 'His words were not fulfilled' means only his first words failed. His last words came true.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The case is where he said, 'And also, if it is not so-and-so, I will be a נזיר.' So what does 'his words were not fulfilled' mean? His first words were not fulfilled, but his last words were.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the earlier question: how can the person whose condition failed become a נזיר? He explains that this person had also said he would be a נזיר even if the condition failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a failed condition should mean no נזירות at all. אביי adds a second statement to the case: 'even if it's not him, I'm a נזיר.' Now the phrase 'not fulfilled' points only to the first statement, and the נזירות comes from the second statement, which did come true.

keyTerms.meaning: for example, where he said; it describes the exact case

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the person 'whose words were not fulfilled' is a נזיר because of his second statement, 'even if it is not so-and-so.' His first statement failed, but his second came true.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think בית הלל make someone a נזיר because his condition failed. He is a נזיר only because of the extra statement אביי adds to the case.

phrases.english: Abaye said: For example, where he said:

phrases.aramaic: ״אִי נָמֵי לָאו פְּלוֹנִי הוּא — אִי הָוֵי נָזִיר״.
phrases.english: "Even if it is not so-and-so, I shall be a nazir."
And what is meant by "his words were not fulfilled"?
His first words were not fulfilled,
but rather his last words were.
phrases.notes: He means: his last words were fulfilled, and that is why he is a נזיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section of the גמרא: how can someone whose words were not fulfilled be a נזיר?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the speaker made an additional statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase seemed to mean that he becomes a נזיר because his condition failed, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said a second statement, 'even if it is not so-and-so,' and that statement was fulfilled. Only his first words failed.

steps.title: From 'he turned back' the גמרא infers that identification would make a nazir
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the approaching man turned back, no one is a נזיר. It infers that if he had come close and been identified, someone would be a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he turned back, no one is a נזיר. The reason is only because he turned back. This implies that if he came toward us and was identified, the one who made the vow would be a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and makes an inference from it. If no one is a נזיר only because the man turned back, then had he come forward, someone would be a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a specific reason why no one is a נזיר: the man was never identified. The גמרא reads closely and concludes that identification is the only thing missing. Once the man is identified, the vow takes effect, even though at the moment of speaking the speaker didn't know for sure who it was.

keyTerms.meaning: came before us (came close and was identified)

steps.whyThisMatters: This inference sets up a question. The vow depended on something unknown when it was made, and it only becomes clear later. Not every opinion accepts that such a vow works.

phrases.english: If he turned back, he is not a nazir, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about the man everyone was guessing about; 'etc.' means the rest of the line.

phrases.english: The reason is because he turned back,
but if he came before us, [the one who vowed] would be a nazir.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּהִרְתִּיעַ לַאֲחוֹרָיו, הָא אָתֵי לְקַמַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a close reading of the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the approaching person is later identified, the vow that depended on his identity takes effect.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that a vow can depend on something only clarified later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא's opinion matches the inference it just made. This is a setup question, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from step 2 assumes that a נזירות vow works even when the speaker didn't know for sure at the time whether his condition was true. Not every תנא may agree, so the גמרא wants to know whose view the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: who is it? (which תנא holds this?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source opinion behind the inference made in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the vow takes effect once the approaching man is identified, as the משנה implies.
